title: Grade 10 Mathematics — Coordinate Geometry
description: Distance formula, section formula, area of triangle, midpoint
subject: mathematics

questions.question: The distance between points A(x₁, y₁) and B(x₂, y₂) is:
questions.explanation: Distance formula: d = √[(x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²]. Derived from Pythagoras' theorem applied to a right triangle with legs (x₂−x₁) and (y₂−y₁).

questions.question: Find the distance between A(3, 4) and B(0, 0).
The midpoint of the line segment joining A(x₁, y₁) and B(x₂, y₂) is:
questions.explanation: Midpoint formula: M = ((x₁+x₂)/2, (y₁+y₂)/2). The midpoint is the average of the x-coordinates and the average of the y-coordinates.

questions.question: The Section Formula for a point P dividing AB (A(x₁,y₁), B(x₂,y₂)) in ratio m:n internally is:
questions.explanation: Internal Section Formula: P = ((mx₂ + nx₁)/(m+n), (my₂ + ny₁)/(m+n)). For m=n=1 (midpoint): P = ((x₁+x₂)/2, (y₁+y₂)/2). Memory: multiply m with B's coordinates.

The area of a triangle with vertices A(x₁,y₁), B(x₂,y₂), C(x₃,y₃) is:
questions.explanation: Area = (1/2)|x₁(y₂−y₃) + x₂(y₃−y₁) + x₃(y₁−y₂)|. The absolute value ensures a positive result. If area = 0, the three points are collinear.

questions.question: If the area of triangle ABC is 0, it means A, B, C are:
options: The vertices of a right triangle
questions.explanation: Area = 0 means the three points lie on a single straight line (collinear). No 'triangle' is formed — the points are co-linear. This is used to test for collinearity.

questions.question: The coordinates of the centroid of a triangle with vertices A(x₁,y₁), B(x₂,y₂), C(x₃,y₃) are:
questions.explanation: Centroid G = ((x₁+x₂+x₃)/3, (y₁+y₂+y₃)/3). The centroid is the point of intersection of medians, located 2/3 of the way from each vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

questions.question: Find the area of triangle with vertices A(0,0), B(4,0), C(0,3).
questions.explanation: Area = (1/2)|0(0−3) + 4(3−0) + 0(0−0)| = (1/2)|0 + 12 + 0| = 6 sq units. (Or simply: right triangle, base 4, height 3: area = ½ × 4 × 3 = 6.)
